title: Multi Game Interpreter
body: A browser based interpreter for eight classic adventure game engine families — LucasArts SCUMM, Sierra AGI and SCI, Adventure Soft AGOS, and Revolution’s Sky, Lure and both Broken Swords. Written from scratch in TypeScript against the original file formats, it runs the games’ own bytecode on a canvas with no plugins, no WebAssembly and no server. It ships with no game data: you point it at files from a copy you own, and nothing leaves your machine. Built end to end with AI assistance across the full software lifecycle — design, implementation, test and documentation.

title: Soundcheck
body: A music creation app — a DAW — whose Assistant, an LLM co-producer, can both edit and listen to your song. The Audio Engine is written in Rust and the UI in React: the desktop app runs the engine natively on the audio device through Tauri, and the lighter Browser Version runs the same engine as WebAssembly in an AudioWorklet, with nothing to install. Tracks, a Timeline, a Step Sequencer, Instruments, recording, a Mixer and WAV or MP3 export, with every edit undoable. Built to WCAG 2.2 AA across its dark and light themes and six colour palettes. Built end to end with AI assistance across the full software lifecycle — design, implementation, test and documentation.

title: Lanewise
body: A free, open source desktop Git client for Windows and macOS, laid out as GitKraken is. A Commit graph draws the whole history in coloured lanes, with branches, tags, stashes and open Pull Requests beside it, and merge conflicts are resolved in a three way view of Base, Ours and Theirs, one Conflict Hunk at a time, with AI Suggestions from your own Model Provider that are never applied for you. The core is written in Rust and the UI in React, running natively through Tauri, with sign in to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps, Issues from Jira Cloud and Trello, no telemetry and WCAG 2.2 AA throughout. Built end to end with AI assistance across the full software lifecycle — design, implementation, test and documentation.

title: AI Office
body: A 3D office where AI agents work your GitHub issues. Each repository is a Floor with a Manager and a team of Agents — coder, reviewer, QA, docs and designer — and you can click a monitor to watch an Agent's sandbox as it works, read the plan on the whiteboard, or simply ask the Manager for a change: it files the issues and brings in contractors for the work. A built in AI Gateway load balances the Agents' requests across your own AI accounts, Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Grok and more, with token caps per office, Floor and Agent, and every request's tokens, cost and timings in Analytics. A TypeScript monorepo with a React and Three.js front end, a Node server, Postgres and Docker sandboxes. Built end to end with AI assistance across the full software lifecycle — design, implementation, test and documentation.

title: Location Scout
body: Pick any location in England — a postcode, an address or a click on the map — and see everything around it on one screen. An interactive map layers crime with its year on year trend, planning constraints and applications, amenities, schools with Ofsted ratings, transport, green space, property sales and EPCs, land and demographics, beside a Location Overview of Good, Watch and Concern Highlights and transparent 0–100 scores, each with its breakdown. Scout Modes reweight the scores for homebuyers, landlords, investors, developers and businesses, and a Land Opportunity Finder surfaces open land with its indicative ownership. React and MapLibre GL in front of a Hono backend, with DuckDB over GeoParquet for land data, optional AI Explanations of the scores and WCAG 2.2 AA throughout. Built end to end with AI assistance across the full software lifecycle — design, implementation, test and documentation.

title: Xray
body: Turns compiled .NET applications back into buildable, runnable C# solutions. Point it at a .exe, a .dll or a folder of them and Xray decompiles the code, resolves each dependency to the framework, a NuGet package, a sibling project or a copied binary, generates an SDK style Visual Studio solution and verifies it with dotnet build — recovering WPF XAML from BAML and Windows Forms designers along the way. A local web UI shows each stage as it runs, lets you browse the recovered C# and XAML and download it as a zip, and every Reconstruction reports honestly whether it is Full or Partial, and why. A TypeScript CLI and web UI over a C# engine, running only on your machine. Built end to end with AI assistance across the full software lifecycle — design, implementation, test and documentation.

title: Media Centre
body: One remote for your whole home. Control your TVs, air conditioners, lights, heating, Amazon Echos and Ring doorbells room by room, and play the films, shows and music on your PC or NAS on any TV, from any phone, tablet or computer on your home network. An always on Hub, on a PC or in Docker on a NAS, serves the Remote, controls every Appliance locally where it can and streams Media Files to a Player it installs on each Samsung TV, converting with ffmpeg whatever the TV cannot play. The Remote adds a floor plan of your Rooms, Light Scenes, Resume Positions and a scan of every device on the network, installs to a home screen and meets WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark — all on your own Hub, with no account. A TypeScript monorepo with a Preact Remote, a Node Hub and a Tizen Player. Built end to end with AI assistance across the full software lifecycle — design, implementation, test and documentation.

title: Belvoir Care
body: A single page marketing site for BelvoirCare Ltd, who have provided bespoke event medical cover across the UK since 2012. Built deliberately with no build step and no dependencies — plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript — with light, dark and system themes applied before first paint so the page never flashes the wrong one. Verified against WCAG 2.2 Level AA with axe-core at 1440px, 390px and 320px.

title: A B Electrical & Maintenance
body: A single page marketing site for A. B. Electrical & Maintenance, a NAPIT-registered and TrustMark-approved electrician working across Nottinghamshire, Derbyshire and the wider East Midlands for over 25 years. Built with no build step and no dependencies — plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript — with light, dark and system themes applied before first paint, an installable web manifest, and an in-page accessibility panel that can switch the motion off. Built to WCAG 2.2 Level AA.

title: Pacman
body: A desktop remake of the arcade original, written in C# as a Windows application and unit tested throughout with NUnit. The ghosts hunt the player around the maze as they do in the 1980 game.

title: Fishy
body: A browser game about the food chain: eat the fish smaller than you, and avoid everything bigger, because the rule cuts both ways. Written in TypeScript and React with SCSS, built with Vite, and published to GitHub Pages on every release.

title: Frogger
body: A remake of the arcade original — get the frog across the traffic and over the river to reach home. Built in TypeScript and React with Vite, and it measures the screen it loads on and scales to fit, so it plays on a phone as readily as a desktop.

title: Space Invaders
body: The fixed shooter remade for the browser: a laser cannon tracking left and right along the bottom, rows of aliens descending and speeding up as their numbers fall, and bunkers that erode from both sides as the shooting goes on. TypeScript, React 19 and Vite, with Vitest over the game logic.

title: Mine Sweeper
body: The classic logic puzzle rebuilt for the browser: open every cell that is not a mine, working out where they are from the neighbour counts alone. Flagging and shift-click chording both work as they did in the original. TypeScript and React with Vite and SCSS.

title: Tetris
body: The falling-block puzzle in TypeScript and React — fill a horizontal line to clear it, and clear several at once for considerably more. Built with Vite, and released and deployed to GitHub Pages straight from the commit history by semantic-release.

title: Connect 4
body: Two-player Connect Four in the browser: drop counters down the grid and be the first to line four up horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Written in TypeScript with React 19, Vite and SCSS.

title: Ant Run
body: A maze runner where you steer an ant along a network of paths and a single step into empty space kills it. The holes around the edge of the board teleport it to the opposite side, which is as often the way out as the way into trouble. TypeScript, React, Vite and SCSS.

title: Pipeline
body: A remake of two BBC Micro favourites, Pipeline and Repton: guide Repton around the field collecting every star while working through gates, keys, boulders and teleports. Built in TypeScript and React 19, and it ships its own level editor — press `e` in play to edit the map, `m` to see it whole.

title: Racer
body: A top-down racing game: hold the car on the track, off the grass and past the other traffic, while oil spills take the grip out from under you. TypeScript and React with Vite and SCSS.

title: Battleships
body: Two-player Battleships split across a game and a server of its own. Each player places five ships, then the guessing starts and neither can move afterwards. Moves travel between the two browsers over Socket.io on an Express back end, with the front end in TypeScript and React.

title: Chuckie Egg
body: A remake of the 1983 platformer. As Hen-House Harry you collect twelve eggs a level against a countdown, dodging the hens patrolling the platforms and the lifts that will carry you off the top of the screen if you ride them too far. TypeScript, React 19 and Vite.

title: Free Cell
body: The solitaire variant where almost every deal can be won, rebuilt in vanilla TypeScript on a canvas with no framework at all. The rules — card, deck, hand and stack — are kept deliberately free of DOM calls so they can be tested in Node without a browser, and ESLint enforces that separation rather than trusting it.

title: Pairs
body: The memory game: turn two cards at a time, keep the pairs that match and put the rest back. Written in vanilla TypeScript on a canvas with no framework, built with Vite and tested with Vitest.

title: Treasure Hunt
body: A team-built augmented reality treasure hunt for mobile. Players follow clues to real-world points of interest, with GPS telling them how far they are from the next one and the camera showing what is waiting there. Unity and Vuforia drive the AR, C# and Swift the device, and a Ruby and Sinatra back end sits over Postgres and MongoDB. The final group project of a Makers Academy cohort.

title: Portfolio
body: This site. A single page portfolio in TypeScript and React 19 covering my career, education, projects and interests, built with Vite and tested with Vitest. Themed light, dark or by system preference, and held to WCAG 2.2 Level AA by an axe-core sweep that runs on every commit.
